issues.legal_issue: A vacant site separately let from a residential building is land rather than a building or its appurtenant land for purposes of the tenant-protection definitions.
material_facts: The landlord retained the residential building and let only its vacant backyard to the tenant.
The lease did not include the building with the site.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was a tenant of land within the Act’s definition, not a tenant of a building.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(1) and 2(2) distinguish a building, including its appurtenances, from land. Because the building was retained and the vacant site was let separately, the letting was of land and nothing else.

predicates.statutory_tenancy_classification_case: The dispute concerns whether a person renting a vacant site qualifies as a tenant of land for statutory tenant protections.
predicates.vacant_site_was_leased: The landlord let a vacant site to the tenant.
predicates.building_was_retained_separately: The landlord retained the building and did not let it together with the site.

issues.definition: When a statutory tenancy-classification dispute concerns a vacant site let separately from a retained building, the tenant is a tenant of land.

issues.legal_issue: A condition requiring removal of a structure that the tenant was authorized to build does not constitute a stipulation as to the erection of buildings that displaces statutory tenant protections.
material_facts: The registered lease authorized the tenant to erect a temporary shed.
The lease required the tenant to dismantle that shed when vacating the site.
issues.conclusion: The dismantling condition was not protected as a stipulation as to the erection of buildings, so that condition alone did not prevent the tenant from claiming statutory protection for the authorized structure.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 12 protects registered written stipulations as to the erection of buildings, not a condition requiring vacant possession after demolition of a building the tenant was authorized to construct. The Court relied on Vajrapani Naidu v. New Theatre Carnatic Talkies and Vajrapuri v. New Theatres Carnatic Talkies.

predicates.statutory_tenant_protection_claim: The tenant seeks statutory protection in a dispute concerning the tenant’s occupation and structures on leased land.
predicates.lease_authorizes_temporary_structure: The lease authorizes the tenant to erect a temporary structure on the land.
predicates.lease_requires_removal_when_vacating: The lease requires the tenant to remove the authorized structure when vacating the land.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks statutory protection, the lease authorizes a temporary structure, and the lease requires its removal on vacating, that removal condition does not bar protection for the authorized structure.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who breaches a registered stipulation prohibiting permanent structures cannot claim compensation for those structures or the associated right to purchase the land.
material_facts: The registered lease expressly prohibited the tenant from erecting permanent structures so as to claim their future value.
The tenant erected permanent structures in breach of that stipulation.
The tenant sought the statutory right to purchase the land in an ejectment suit.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not entitled to compensation for the permanent structures and, consequently, could not claim the statutory right to purchase the land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 9 are controlled by section 12. The proviso to section 12 preserves registered written stipulations as to the erection of buildings, including a stipulation prohibiting permanent structures. A tenant who builds in breach of such a stipulation cannot obtain compensation under section 3 and therefore cannot obtain the benefit of section 9. The Court distinguished R.V. Naidu v. Naraindas, where the covenant was unregistered, and referred to Naraindas v. V. Naidu.

predicates.ejectment_and_land_purchase_claim: A tenant facing an ejectment suit claims a statutory right to purchase the leased land.
predicates.registered_lease_prohibits_permanent_str: A registered lease expressly prohibits the tenant from erecting permanent structures.
predicates.tenant_built_permanent_structures_in_bre: The tenant erected permanent structures in breach of the lease prohibition.

issues.definition: When an ejectment defendant claims a right to purchase land, the registered lease prohibits permanent structures, and the tenant builds them in breach, the tenant lacks compensation and land-purchase rights for those structures.
